decision: When Trust Magnitude has zero effective evidence rows, may Steward infer or propose a demotion from the empty pool?
whyItMatters: An empty pool can be a sensor or context omission (#2114), a collection failure, or a genuine absence; treating it as degradation would mass-demote skills on missing data.
evidence: Founder ruling 2026-10-28 (#2201): no. Check canonical effective evidence including inheritance, search for admissible new evidence, recalculate from qualifying evidence, and if none remains preserve the existing rating pending a governed decision. No bulk calibration.
37 of 51 open trust_calibration_drift debts were empty-pool demotion proposals on 2026-10-28.
Implemented as a sensor evidence-gap observation without a target level or calibration command (founder/steward/decisions/LEDGER.md row 9).
recommended: Preserve the stored rating; report an evidence gap; never auto-demote on absence. A demotion needs actual counter-evidence or supersession under #2148.
alternative: Treat an empty pool as ungraded and demote (rejected by the founder).
unblocks: Retiring the empty-pool demotion proposals; evidence discovery as the next step (see steward-trust-evidence-gap-kind).
